---
title: "Formatting Values"
guide-section: "Using tinytab"
---

tinytab has three functions for turning a single number into a display string. They share the
same rules: the value is the first argument, and every option is a keyword argument.

## Numbers

[`fmt_number()`](../reference/fmt_number.qmd) rounds to a fixed number of decimal places (2 by
default) and groups thousands with a separator:

```{python}
from tinytab import fmt_number

fmt_number(1234567.891)
```

Use `decimals=` to change the precision:

```{python}
fmt_number(1234567.891, decimals=0)
```

The thousands separator is a comma by default. Set another with `sep_mark=`:

```{python}
fmt_number(1234567.891, sep_mark=" ")
```

## Percentages

[`fmt_percent()`](../reference/fmt_percent.qmd) takes a proportion, where `1` means 100%, and
shows one decimal place by default:

```{python}
from tinytab import fmt_percent

fmt_percent(0.256)
```

```{python}
fmt_percent(0.256, decimals=0)
```

## Currencies

[`fmt_currency()`](../reference/fmt_currency.qmd) adds a currency symbol and uses the right
number of decimal places for the currency. US dollars are the default:

```{python}
from tinytab import fmt_currency

fmt_currency(1234.5)
```

Choose another currency with a three-letter code (in any case). Yen are shown without decimal
places, and negative amounts put the sign before the symbol:

```{python}
[
    fmt_currency(1234.5, currency="eur"),
    fmt_currency(1234.5, currency="JPY"),
    fmt_currency(-5, currency="GBP"),
]
```

The supported codes are USD, EUR, GBP, and JPY. Any other code is an error, and the message
lists the valid ones:

```{python}
#| error: true
fmt_currency(10, currency="XYZ")
```

## Only numbers

All three functions accept only numbers (integers and floats). Anything else, including a
number written as a string, raises a `TypeError`:

```{python}
#| error: true
fmt_number("10")
```

`True` and `False` are rejected too, even though Python treats them as the integers 1 and 0.
Formatting a boolean as "1.00" is almost always a mistake.
